# for-each Loop

#### Course: Learn Java Basics

## for-each Loop

So far, we have been using the for loop to access each element of the array.

In Java, there is another variation of the for loop called the for-each loop. It makes accessing array elements really easy. Let's see an example.

```java
1class Main {
2    public static void main(String[] args) {
3        
4        // Create an array
5        int numbers[] = {35, 42, 56, 62, 67};
6        
7        // Access each element using for each-loop 
8        for (int number : numbers) {
9            System.out.println(number);
10        }
11    }
12}
```

Output

```text
35
42
56
62
67
```

In the program,

- for - syntax of the loop
- numbers - name of the array
- int number - temporary variable. You can name this variable anything you want.

The loop iterates 5 times because the array has 5 elements. In each iteration, the element of the array is assigned to the number variable. Hence, we get the element when we print number.

Here's how the code works:

| Iteration | number | Loop Body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1st | 35 | Prints 35 |
| 2nd | 42 | Prints 42 |
| 3rd | 56 | Prints 56 |
| 4th | 62 | Prints 62 |
| 5th | 67 | Prints 67 |
